text: I see the chest skin lesion you're referring to; can you tell me when you first noticed it and if it has changed in size, color, or shape since then? Also, have you experienced any pain, itching, or bleeding from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your age and the lesion's growth over two months, has this spot ever changed color, bled, or crusted? Additionally, do you recall any recent trauma to that area, or does it appear raised and firm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual for a chest lesion to suggest appendicitis; could you clarify if the previous doctor misdiagnosed the location or if you are confusing two different medical issues? Given the lesion's growth and your history of diabetes, I am concerned about malignancy or an infected ulcer. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, REQUEST TEST: Lesion_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: NORMAL READINGS; LESION_BIOPSY: Histopathology_Findings: Atypical melanocytes that infiltrate the epidermis and dermis, confirming the diagnosis of malignant melanoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Melanoma. Given the biopsy results showing atypical melanocytes and your history of diabetes, I recommend requesting images of the lesion to document its specific morphology and check for satellite lesions.
